tool: M5.F recorder: DouyinSite(IoLiveHttp()).getRoomDetail for each room (anonymous), then DouyinDanmakuConnection with a connector that logs every frame; five rooms at once for 150 s
note: Anonymous and read-only, direct. Five live rooms of the 聊天 and 音乐 partitions picked by size (the detail's exact audience 2, 5, 2013, 9812 and 77726), recorded at the same time. Kept: the frames of each room's first 60 s that carry a chat (WebcastChatMessage) or an audience message (WebcastRoomUserSeqMessage), with only those messages; t is milliseconds since that room's capturedAt, the room is the line's `room` (web_rid). Each message was reduced to the fields the decoder reads (chat: common without its user, user, content, eventTime; audience: common, total 3, totalUser 7, totalUserStr 8, totalStr 9, onlineUserForAnchor 10, totalPvForAnchor 11); PushFrame fields (headers, logId, encoding) and Response fields (cursor, now, internalExt, needAck) are as recorded, and a gzip payload is gzipped again. Senders became synthetic: a random id of the same length and 观众N, one per id and name in a room; Douyin's placeholder id 111111, which it gives viewers shown with a masked name (敏***), is kept. @-mentions in chat text became @观众. What it shows (docs/modules/M5.4-douyin.md, 后续升级): in every room total is the exact number the text rounds (2 and '2', 5 and '5', 1986 and '1986', 10371 and '1.0万', 77918 and '7.8万'); no chat has common.createTime, every chat has eventTime, 0.8 to 14.2 s before it arrived; 8 of the 333 chats came again about 0.6 s later with the same msgId.
